description: A two-draw tree for an urn with replacement: each draw branches to blue (8 of 11) or red (3 of 11). The four terminal frequencies are 64 BB, 24 BR, 24 RB, and 9 RR, totaling 121.

A two-draw tree for face and non-face cards with replacement: the first draw has 12 face cards and 40 non-face cards, and each second draw has the same counts. Terminal frequencies are 144 FF, 480 FN, 480 NF, and 1,600 NN.
A two-draw urn tree without replacement. The branches start with blue 8/11 and red 3/11; after drawing red, only 2 red marbles remain out of 10, and the four terminal probabilities sum to 110/110.

A two-draw tree for face and non-face cards without replacement. First-draw branches are F 12/52 and N 40/52; after F, second-draw branches are F 11/51 and N 40/51; after N, they are F 12/51 and N 39/51.
A Venn diagram for two fair coin tosses: A is tails on the first coin and B is tails on the second. TT lies in the overlap, TH lies only in A, HT lies only in B, and HH lies outside both.
A Venn diagram with overlapping circles C (belongs to a club) and PT (works part time). The accompanying example gives P(C)=0.40, P(PT)=0.50, and P(C and PT)=0.05.
A tree for tossing a coin and drawing one bead: H has probability 2/3 and T has probability 1/3; each coin branch then splits into red, yellow, and blue beads with probabilities 3/12, 4/12, and 5/12.
A two-card tree with replacement: each draw branches to green 5/8 or yellow 3/8. The joint outcome GG has probability 25/64.

A Pareto bar chart of De Anza student ethnicity, ordered from largest to smallest: Asian 36.1%, White 24.5%, Hispanic/Latino 17.1%, Other/Unknown 9.6%, Black 5.8%, Filipino 5.3%, Pacific Islander 1.0%, and Native American 0.6%.
A symmetric histogram with values 4 through 10, centered at 7; the bars mirror around 7 and the mean, median, and mode are all 7.
A histogram for values 4 through 8 with a longer tail on the left; it is skewed to the left.
A histogram for values 6 through 10 with a longer tail on the right; it is skewed to the right.
A uniform-distribution graph has a constant-height density from x=2 to x=9, with the area between x=3 and x=6 shaded.
An exponential-distribution curve decreases from left to right, with the area between x=2 and x=4 shaded.
A standard normal bell curve has the area between x=1 and x=2 shaded.
Three lines y=a+bx are shown: b>0 slopes upward to the right, b=0 is horizontal, and b<0 slopes downward to the right.
Three scatterplots compare correlation signs: panel (a) is positive, panel (b) is negative, and panel (c) has zero correlation.
